title: The Vine and the Vineyard
lead: Israel is pictured as God's vine or vineyard, brought out of Egypt and planted in the land, then broken down when it bears no fruit. Jesus takes up the image in his parable of the tenants and calls himself the true vine.

sections.b: The image begins with a farmer's care: God brings a vine out of Egypt, clears the ground and plants it (Psalm 80:8–11). The prophets turn it into judgment: Isaiah's song of the vineyard that yielded sour grapes (Isaiah 5:1–7), Jeremiah's choice vine turned wild (Jeremiah 2:21), Ezekiel's useless vine wood (Ezekiel 15) and uprooted vine (Ezekiel 19:10–14), Hosea's luxuriant vine (Hosea 10:1). Jesus' parable of the tenants begins with Isaiah's vineyard (Mark 12:1–9), and in John 15:1–8 he says, "I am the true vine", with his followers as the branches.
